solutions.title: Force both trigonometric factors to equal one
solutions.explanation:
For both logarithms to be defined, their arguments must be positive. Since sine and cosine never exceed \(1\), we have
\[
0<\sin(3\theta)\le1,\qquad
0<\cos(2\theta)\le1.
\]
Combining the logarithms gives
\[
\log\bigl(\sin(3\theta)\cos(2\theta)\bigr)=0,
\]
so
\[
\sin(3\theta)\cos(2\theta)=1.
\]
Two positive numbers at most \(1\) can have product \(1\) only if both equal \(1\). Thus we need
\[
\sin(3\theta)=1,\qquad \cos(2\theta)=1.
\]
Because \(0\le2\theta\le4\pi\), the cosine condition gives
\[
2\theta\in\{0,2\pi,4\pi\},
\qquad \theta\in\{0,\pi,2\pi\}.
\]
At each of these angles, \(\sin(3\theta)=0\), so none satisfies the required sine condition. There are \(\boxed{0}\) solutions, choice \(\text{A}\).
